title: Support Operations Analysis Report
executive_summary: Analysis of 347 support tickets reveals a total labor cost of $27,422.84 and a mean resolution time of ~75 minutes. Team Beta incurs the highest labor cost, phone is the fastest channel, and email tickets reopen at more than twice the rate of chat tickets. A small high-cost, low-satisfaction segment warrants targeted intervention, and workload is reasonably distributed across 18 agents.

key_findings.statement: The dataset contains 347 tickets with a mean resolution time of 75.2 minutes and a total labor cost of $27,422.84.
Team Beta incurred the highest labor cost at $10,247.32, followed by Gamma at $9,387.74 and Alpha at $7,787.78.
Chat had the longest mean resolution time at 83.0 minutes, followed by email at 73.0 minutes; phone was fastest at 69.3 minutes.
Email tickets have a reopening rate of 17.2% versus 7.8% for chat—an increase of ~119.8% relative to chat, indicating email resolutions are far less durable.
12 tickets meet the high-cost (≥$100), low-satisfaction (score ≤2) criteria; of these, 8.3% were reopened, suggesting this segment has moderate but notable rework risk.

Resolution time has a median of 65 minutes and a standard deviation of 51.9 minutes, indicating a right-skewed distribution. Mean satisfaction (where recorded) is 4.15 out of 5, with 19 tickets missing a satisfaction score.

18 distinct agents handled the 347 tickets. The busiest single agent handled 26 tickets, representing a 7.5% share of total volume—suggesting workload is reasonably distributed with no severe concentration.

limitations: 19 tickets are missing satisfaction scores, which may introduce bias into the satisfaction mean if missingness is non-random (e.g., correlated with poor outcomes).
Labor cost is derived from logged resolution minutes and assumed hourly rates; inaccuracies in time-tracking or rate assumptions would propagate into all cost metrics.
The dataset represents a single export snapshot; trends over time cannot be assessed without longitudinal data.
Reopening rates are computed per channel but not controlled for ticket complexity or priority, so channel differences may partly reflect ticket-mix rather than channel quality.
Agent concentration analysis uses ticket count only; tickets vary in complexity and duration, so count-based share may understate or overstate true workload concentration.
conclusion: Overall support performance is solid—satisfaction averages 4.15 and the top agent holds only 7.5% of volume—but two areas need attention: email's reopening rate is 120% higher than chat's, and Team Beta accounts for the largest labor spend at $10,247. Reducing email rework and investigating Beta's cost drivers should be the immediate operational priorities.
